figures.finding: Belgium's federal Tax Shelter (since 2003) is not a fixed-rate rebate: certified Belgian (co-)producers raise money from Belgian companies that receive tax certificates, against an obligation to spend eligible audiovisual expenses in Belgium and the EEA within 18 months (24 for animation); producers net between 38% and 40% of eligible Belgian expenditure, and investors earn 12-month Euribor plus 450 basis points for up to 18 months.

value.name: Tax Shelter
value.eligibleProducer: Belgian company whose main purpose is audiovisual production, not a broadcaster

figures.applies: Belgium, European works and treaty co-productions with a certified Belgian producer.

sources.said: Unlike many other incentive systems within Europe, the Tax Shelter is not a cash or tax rebate expressed as a fixed percentage. … producers can finance between 38% and 40% of eligible Belgian expenditure through the Tax Shelter mechanism. … This interest is calculated according to the average 12-month Euribor rate, increased by 450 basis points, over a maximum period of 18 months. … the Belgian (co-)producer must make the eligible expenses within 18 months (24 months for animation) of signing the framework agreement. … The Belgian Tax Shelter system has been in place since 2003

figures.finding: Flanders' economic fund Screen Flanders has an annual budget of €3.5 million over two calls and awards at most €400,000 per feature or series, as refundable advances on net receipts; cultural support comes from the Flanders Audiovisual Fund (VAF) and the French-speaking Community's CCA, and in Brussels screen.brussels invested more than €3 million in 29 projects in 2023.

cultural: Centre du Cinéma et de l'Audiovisuel (Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles)

figures.applies: Belgium; Screen Flanders as published 2026; screen.brussels results for 2023.

sources.said: With an annual budget of 3.5 million euros, spread over two separate calls … Belgian producers can apply for support for fiction, animation and documentary features and series for a maximum amount of 400,000 euros. The support is awarded as refundable advances on net receipts.
This year, more than 3 million euros were invested in 29 projects that should generate at least 24 million euros in direct audiovisual expenditure.
the CCA in the French-speaking part of Belgium, and with the Netherlands Film Fund.
